doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Touring, Ella Fitzgerald and South America
title: Tango versus bossa nova
summary: Hall distinguishes South American musics and says he couldn't imitate them, criticizing the Getz/Byrd records.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well, just before we took the break, we were sort of in Buenos Aires. That’s where we left off.

And I asked sort of a dumb question, which was, did it influence your playing when you got home. And I mean, obviously it would in some way. But what I’m really curious about is that that was a few years really before Stan Getz’s recording and…
Yeah, Stan did kind of bossa nova stuff from, from Brazil. I’m sorry, go ahead.
Okay. Mo, but that’s a good distinction.
I was sort of lumping the whole South American influence together, and really what you’re saying is that I shouldn’t. So that’s a good distinction for me to understand.
Sambas and tangos. Tango music is really quite different, I think. It’s like Count Basie and Stravinsky or something. (laughs)
So that you, do you see it… is there any relationship in that sort of migration, though, of the South American music influence in American music and in jazz that came about in the early sixties?

I’m sure there was. I know… Well, I guess it’s like any experience in one’s life. Unless you’re a complete idiot, it affects you somehow. And it broadens your perception of whatever it is you’re doing. And I know that Charlie Byrd and Stan Getz did these kinda fake Brazilian… (laughs) They were sort of bossa novas, I guess. It was a bit hammy. And my friends from Brazil said that they used to laugh about those records. (laughs) You know… It would feel the same if I tried to imitate, or if I tried to imitate flamenco or whatever. I’m a gringo. (laughs) I can’t do that. It’s not my fault, really, and it’s too much… I can’t play like Freddy Green, either. I could probably come closer to Freddy than bossa nova, though. ‘Cause it’s more stateside music that I’ve had experience with.
